chapter: Cliff Jackson, Jelly Roll Morton and Harlem in the 1920s
title: A second audition ruined by Jelly Roll and the song plugger
summary: At an audition near Roseland, Jelly Roll recognised the promoter, a former song plugger, and insulted him about his fur coat.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Well now, the climax of it, we had another audition right up here near the Roseland Ballroom, Jelly sold was the NBC Studio, (unintelligible) the fellows out. And here, and we'd been working I got another chance. (Unintelligible) people work around with you, gigging, you know. So I said, all right, what it going to be, Jelly? It's just going to be a good show, be very prompt, good show, and you cats got to play like (unintelligible). Said, yeah, I hope you don't do what you did like the Apollo Parlor Theater. Hap, don't talk that way. I said, well, I'm going to talk that way because you messed it up.

Ain't going to be that way. I said, all right. Get down there and rehearse, everything was fine. The fellow was supposed to promote the show, he came in, little guy no bigger than, taller than me. So after (unintelligible) and the man hears as he says I'll wait until the big man comes, and you promote the band and the show. So when the man walked in, it's funny, he had a big fur coat on way down almost to his ankles, a racoon coat.

Jelly said, I know that guy. I say, wait a minute. Are you sure you know him? I know him. I said, Jelly, don't do that Apollo Theater now. You know him? Sure, I know him. So he went up to Hop? (unintelligible) and said, what's the matter over there? I said, well, Jelly says you know him. This is what Jelly did to the man. Fellow took off his coat, laid it down, says, I want to listen to the band. The band got up and said, 'hey, don't I know you?' So he said, 'I don't think you do.' Said, 'yes, you do.' So you didn't have that for coat on before, he caught on, what I saw, when I knew you, you used to bring music around to the dance-halls and ballrooms, which that time they called pluggers. See?
The man said, you don't know me. Says, you didn't have no fur coat on then, fellow. I said, oh, my goodness. Here he goes again. Lost that one.
